page: Amazon Web Services c6in.24xlarge is a high-throughput, compute-optimized instance hosted on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by 3rd Generation Intel Xeon Scalable 8375C processors running on an x86_64 architecture at 3.5 GHz. The configuration allocates 96 dedicated vCPUs derived from 48 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading, backed by 54 MB of L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 192.0 GB of DDR4 running at 3 GHz, establishing a 1:2 memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated local SSD storage or discrete GPU hardware, routing all persistent disk I/O through Amazon Elastic Block Store. A core architectural characteristic is its baseline network throughput of 150 Gbps.

Benchmark results highlight strong multi-core computational throughput alongside median single-core performance. The instance achieved top-quartile scores in multi-threaded stress-ng evaluation (92,860.61) and Geekbench multi-core testing (17,721.0), with particularly strong results in Clang software compilation (55,187.0) and ray tracing (84,707.0). PassMark encryption testing placed in the top decile at 87,331.36, assisted by hardware acceleration instructions including AVX-512 and VAES. Cached memory bandwidth reaches 4,978.67 GB/sec, while large-block read operations sustain 326.86 GB/sec. Conversely, single-thread Geekbench (1,665.0) and stress-ng (1,893.09) scores remain squarely in the median tier, indicating performance gains derive predominantly from parallel execution across all 96 vCPUs.

The qualitative efficiency profile of the c6in.24xlarge favors parallel, network-heavy applications over single-threaded or memory-intensive tasks. The lack of local storage requires architectural reliance on networked block volumes, meaning workloads with extreme local disk IOPS demands may encounter I/O latency bottlenecks. However, the 150 Gbps network pipe offers substantial bandwidth density per compute unit. This profile makes the instance effective for distributed computing clusters, CI/CD software build farms, static web serving, network firewalls, and data-intensive packet processing tasks.
description: Amazon Web Services c6in.24xlarge is a compute-optimized instance running on the AWS Nitro System. Featuring 3rd Generation Intel Xeon 8375C processors clocked at 3.5 GHz, it supplies 96 dedicated vCPUs across 48 physical cores and 192.0 GB of DDR4 system memory. Hardware includes AVX-512 vector extensions and cryptographic accelerators, though it contains no onboard local storage or discrete GPU devices. Its most prominent capability is a 150 Gbps baseline networking interface. Benchmark evaluations demonstrate strong multi-threaded capabilities, placing in the top quartile for PassMark CPU, Geekbench multi-core, and software build tests, complemented by top-tier encryption ratings. Single-core performance falls in the median range. The 2.0 GB per vCPU allocation and substantial network pipe make the instance resource-efficient for parallelized, high-throughput network applications, distributed computing pipelines, and CI/CD compilation workloads rather than storage-bound tasks.
